original_question: Find the asymptotic value of phi(n,5,9), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set in which every five-point subset determines at least nine distinct distances.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 32: find the asymptotic value of phi(n,5,9). The immediately preceding k=5 discussion singles out this case and notes Erdős's motivating question of whether phi(n,5,9) = Omega(n^2). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object and the right level of scope: it asks for the asymptotic behavior of phi(n,5,9), keeps the problem planar, and states the correct local hypothesis that every 5-point subset determines at least 9 distinct distances. That is essentially the official open problem in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
missing_details: The ambient space should be stated explicitly as the Euclidean plane R^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
It should be explicit that phi(n,5,9) is a minimum taken over all sets P of n distinct points in R^2 satisfying the local condition. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

It helps to spell out that a 5-point subset determines at least 9 distinct distances means at least 9 distinct values among its 10 pairwise Euclidean distances. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
The asymptotic quantifier should be made explicit as n -> infinity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

The paper imposes no extra general-position assumptions here beyond the five-point distance condition, so the stand-alone version should not accidentally add any. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
refined_question: As n -> infinity, determine the asymptotic growth of phi(n,5,9), where phi(n,5,9) denotes the minimum possible number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by a set P of n distinct points in R^2 such that every 5-point subset Q of P determines at least 9 distinct values among the 10 pairwise distances {|pq| : p,q in Q, p != q}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper, but the nearest official formulation is the paper's named open problem rather than a free paraphrase. In the opening paragraph of Section 7, the paper defines phi(n,k,l) for planar point sets with the local property that every k-point subset determines at least l distinct distances. Then, in the k=5 discussion, it highlights the specific case phi(n,5,9), records Erdős's sharper motivating question phi(n,5,9) = Omega(n^2), and immediately states the official problem as Problem 32: find the asymptotic value of phi(n,5,9). So the paper-faithful refinement should preserve the asymptotic-value formulation while making the definition fully explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
